For a given mean and variance of a general class RVaR, we obtain sharp upper and lower bounds for the worst-case scenarios in single and aggregate risks with given mean and/or variance, as well symmetry and/or unmodality of each marginal risks.

we obtain sharp bounds for the worst-case scenarios for the general class of RVaR under partial information settings, which include the worst-case scenarios under different partial information for VaR and TVaR, as well as the worst-case copulas among the marginal risks.

for a general class of RVaR with given mean and/or variance, symmetry, unimodality, and dependence structure of marginal risks, sharp bounds for the worst-case scenarios are obtained for single risk and aggregate risk models under different partial information scenarios, and the corresponding bounds for VaR and TVaR are also obtained.

, for the worst-case RVaR, we have the following results: (1) the bounds under partial information settings are sharp and (2) the bounds under different partial settings are consistent.

, in the presence of partial information, our results provide the worst-case scenarios and the corresponding sharp bounds for RV a R, which are the most conservative and least informative bounds for VaR, TVaR, and RVaR.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the partial information on the mean and variance of each marginal risk can significantly reduce the range of worst-case scenarios of RVaR, and the partial information on unimodality or symmetry of marginal risks further improves the bounds.

we provide a unified method to derive sharp bounds of a general class risk measures, the RVaR, for single and aggregate risks under various partial information settings, together with the worst-case scenarios for marginal risks and the dependence structures among them.

, for the general class of RVaR and the partial information settings studied in this paper, we provide a unified approach to determine the worst-case scenarios for RVaR and its corresponding copula function, which is of independent interest in its own right.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the partial information setting plays a significant role in determining the worst-case scenarios, which can be useful for risk management.
partial information on the mean and variance of the risk distribution, together with symmetry and/or unmodality of each marginal distribution, is very helpful to obtain tight bounds for VaR and TVaR.

, in general, the partial information of the mean and variance of the marginal risks, as well as that of the dependence structure, can be used to derive sharp bounds for the worst-case scenarios and the corresponding copulas of RVaR.
